scope: Infrastructure & Internet Operations: capacity, resource controls, hardware alternatives and core VM host administration.
status: Research and lab design; no physical-device, hypervisor, load-capacity, storage-stress, or production benchmark executed by this review.
method: Fetched first-party public documentation and official hardware PDFs/official repository sources; read relevant sections. HTTP status, resolved URL and SHA-256 capture each retrieved response. Source support does not prove the proposed learning outcomes or hardware fit.

sources.title: Linux cgroup v2
sources.evidence_type: First-party public documentation inspected; no course lab executed by this source review.
supports: cgroup v2 separates CPU weight from CPU bandwidth limits.
Memory high/max/events and pressure accounting support controlled resource experiments; they do not guarantee dedicated cores or unlimited reclaim.

sources.title: Caddy reverse proxy
sources.evidence_type: First-party public documentation inspected; no course lab executed by this source review.
supports: Caddy reverse_proxy documents selectable load-balancing policies and defaults, active/passive health checks and upstream handling.
A lab should explicitly configure its policy and readiness behaviour, then observe the actual request result.

sources.title: NGINX upstream module
sources.evidence_type: First-party public documentation inspected; no course lab executed by this source review.
supports: NGINX upstream configuration describes weighted round-robin, least connections, failure parameters, connection limits, and edition/version-specific features.

sources.title: k6 open and closed models
sources.evidence_type: First-party public documentation inspected; no course lab executed by this source review.
supports: Closed-user iterations and open arrival-rate execution answer different load questions.
A closed test may reduce its arrival rate when the service becomes slower; documentation discusses coordinated omission.

sources.title: k6 dropped iterations
sources.evidence_type: First-party public documentation inspected; no course lab executed by this source review.
supports: Dropped iterations must be interpreted alongside VU allocation and the system response time; configured arrival rate is not proof of delivered work.

sources.title: Google SRE handling overload
sources.evidence_type: First-party public documentation inspected; no course lab executed by this source review.
supports: A service should handle overload deliberately and protect useful admitted work.
Retry policy, client behaviour and dependency layers influence overload amplification.

sources.title: Google SRE monitoring distributed systems
sources.evidence_type: First-party public documentation inspected; no course lab executed by this source review.
supports: Latency, traffic, errors and saturation are distinct service-monitoring signals.

sources.title: Brendan Gregg USE Method
sources.evidence_type: First-party public documentation inspected; no course lab executed by this source review.
supports: The author documents the Utilization, Saturation and Errors method for finding resource bottlenecks.

sources.title: Prometheus storage
sources.evidence_type: First-party public documentation inspected; no course lab executed by this source review.
supports: Prometheus local storage includes blocks, WAL/head data and compaction behaviour.
Time/size retention and additional compaction headroom are necessary; compressed bytes per sample alone are not a whole-process budget.

sources.title: systemd journald configuration
sources.evidence_type: First-party public documentation inspected; no course lab executed by this source review.
supports: journald offers persistent/volatile storage modes, maximum-use and keep-free limits.
Log storage behaviour has retention, disk and memory tradeoffs.

sources.title: SQLite write ahead logging
sources.evidence_type: First-party public documentation inspected; no course lab executed by this source review.
supports: SQLite WAL supports concurrent readers with one writer and requires same-machine shared-memory semantics.
A long reader can delay checkpoint progress; WAL is not a multi-host replicated database.

sources.title: PostgreSQL resource consumption
sources.evidence_type: First-party public documentation inspected; no course lab executed by this source review.
supports: PostgreSQL work_mem applies per query operation/session and can multiply under concurrency.
Database memory allocations must be understood together with OS cache, pool and parallel-work behaviour.

sources.title: Microsoft advanced WSL configuration
sources.evidence_type: First-party public documentation inspected; no course lab executed by this source review.
supports: WSL2 has host-configured memory, logical-processor, swap and networking behaviour; its available resources differ from physical host resources.

sources.title: Docker multi-platform builds
sources.evidence_type: First-party public documentation inspected; no course lab executed by this source review.
supports: Cross-platform container builds can use emulation, native nodes or cross compilation.
QEMU emulation can be much slower for compilation and compression, so it does not establish native performance.

sources.title: Raspberry Pi 4 product brief
sources.evidence_type: First-party public documentation inspected; no course lab executed by this source review.
supports: Current official Pi 4 product brief documents CPU/RAM choices, Ethernet, USB, microSD and power requirements.
Product specifications are not measurements of the proposed course workload.

sources.title: Raspberry Pi 5 product brief
sources.evidence_type: First-party public documentation inspected; no course lab executed by this source review.
supports: Current official Pi 5 product brief documents ARM CPU, RAM variants, USB/PCIe interfaces and power requirements.
A compatible adapter/power/cooling configuration is part of the whole device profile.

sources.title: Raspberry Pi power supplies
sources.evidence_type: First-party public documentation inspected; no course lab executed by this source review.
supports: Official Raspberry Pi power guidance varies by model and connected peripherals.
Pi 5 downstream USB power allowance differs with compatible supply capability.
Historical manufacturer current measurements have an explicit historical test setup; they are not Ascend measurements.

sources.title: Raspberry Pi frequency management
sources.evidence_type: First-party public documentation inspected; no course lab executed by this source review.
supports: Official Raspberry Pi documentation explains thermal throttling, frequency management, temperature observation and cooling.
sources.access_note: Official documentation source used because the public Raspberry Pi HTML documentation returned HTTP 403 in this environment.

sources.title: Raspberry Pi SD cards
sources.evidence_type: First-party public documentation inspected; no course lab executed by this source review.
supports: Official Raspberry Pi SD-card material describes storage-interface/performance effects and card capability classes.
Published card performance is not a statement about every card endurance or the proposed service benchmark.

sources.evidence_type: First-party public documentation inspected; no course lab executed by this source review.
supports: USB mass-storage boot depends on model, firmware/boot configuration, enclosure compatibility and peripheral power.
sources.access_note: Official documentation source used because the public Raspberry Pi HTML documentation returned HTTP 403 in this environment.

sources.title: Raspberry Pi Zero models
sources.evidence_type: First-party public documentation inspected; no course lab executed by this source review.
supports: Official Zero model documentation distinguishes original single-core 32-bit Zero hardware from quad-core 64-bit Zero 2 W, with 512 MB memory and limited ports.
sources.access_note: Official documentation source used because the public Raspberry Pi HTML documentation returned HTTP 403 in this environment.

sources.title: OpenWrt minimum hardware requirements
sources.evidence_type: First-party public documentation inspected; no course lab executed by this source review.
supports: OpenWrt supported-device guidance requires exact hardware/version support and attention to limited flash/RAM.

sources.title: libvirt virsh command reference
sources.evidence_type: First-party public documentation inspected; no course lab executed by this source review.
supports: virsh exposes guest lifecycle, CPU, memory, storage, network and live/persistent configuration operations.
Live memory changes may use ballooning and CPU changes have guest/hypervisor/maxima constraints.

sources.title: libvirt domain XML
sources.evidence_type: First-party public documentation inspected; no course lab executed by this source review.
supports: libvirt domain XML distinguishes vCPU topology/maxima, boot/current/max memory and optional hotplug/balloon devices.
Hypervisor configuration must be checked against guest-visible state and actual driver support.

sources.title: libvirt virtual network definition
sources.evidence_type: First-party public documentation inspected; no course lab executed by this source review.
supports: libvirt network definitions distinguish isolated, NAT, routed and bridge modes and their addressing/forwarding configuration.

sources.title: cloud-init NoCloud datasource
sources.evidence_type: First-party public documentation inspected; no course lab executed by this source review.
supports: NoCloud supports per-instance metadata/user-data and several ways to supply a local seed.
Instance identity and resulting first-boot configuration must be verified in the cloned guest.

sources.title: Proxmox VE administration guide
sources.evidence_type: First-party public documentation inspected; no course lab executed by this source review.
supports: Proxmox VE provides a host management UI/CLI/API, permissions, storage/network and backup features.
Host hardware/OS requirements and guest allocations are cumulative; supported architecture must be checked for the selected release.

sources.title: Cockpit Machines
sources.evidence_type: First-party public documentation inspected; no course lab executed by this source review.
supports: The official Cockpit Machines project documents a VM UI backed by libvirt-related tooling and virt-install/virt-xml.

proposed_resource_envelopes.status: Unmeasured design envelopes, to validate on each concrete recipe and learner environment.

first_vm_pair.notes: Virtual capacities are not host-space reservations. Include QEMU overhead, observers, snapshots and actual disk allocation.

proposed_resource_envelopes.proposed_small_target_free_space_reserve: max(10 GiB, 20% of usable filesystem), subject to recipe validation and stricter existing reservations.

hardware_coverage: USB SSD and supported NVMe adapter
UPS or explicitly supported battery system
limitations: All resource figures are proposed starting envelopes; no visitor-rate, Pi-wattage or storage-endurance promise is inferred.
One-PC multi-VM results share physical power, storage and uplink and do not establish host HA.
Published product capabilities are version/model dependent; match exact hardware, OS and architecture.
VM hotplug, memory balloon, nesting and networking require a tested host/guest/driver recipe; no blanket compatibility is claimed.
Course effectiveness, effort, accessibility, troubleshooting quality and hardware fit require implemented reference labs and learner pilots.
Local learner reports do not automatically become trusted Ascend assessment receipts.
Some initial guessed source URLs or connections failed; usable official replacements are listed in sources.
